name: TX-36
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Brian Babin running with large cash advantage
Democrat Rhonda Hart has raised no money
model.rationale: Babin is an incumbent in an R+12 district with over $900,000 on hand, while Hart has raised nothing, and prediction markets give the Republican roughly a 93% chance. The fundamentals baseline of about R+15 fits the evidence, so the forecast stays near it.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending in the district would be the first sign the race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-36 is a heavily Republican East Texas district where incumbent Brian Babin is seeking another term after easily winning renomination. The district's partisan lean of R+12 gives Republicans a strong structural advantage, and Babin adds the usual incumbency edge on top of it. He has raised about $1 million and holds roughly $900,000 in cash, giving him a clear financial edge.

Democrat Rhonda Hart faces steep odds: she has reported no fundraising and no cash on hand, and no outside groups have engaged in the race. No public polls are available, but prediction markets price the Republican at about a 93% chance of winning. With no evidence of a competitive race, this sits firmly in Safe R territory.
